title: Bhakti Saints, Acharyas, Nathpanthis, Siddhas, and Yogis
definition: A socio-religious movement spanning the 7th-17th centuries, characterized by the shift from ritualistic Vedic orthodoxy to personal devotion (Bhakti) and esoteric ascetic practices (Nath/Siddha) as paths to liberation.
importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in Prelims (chronology, philosophy, regional distribution) and Mains (socio-cultural impact, synthesis of traditions, and egalitarianism).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Bhakti Saints Acharyas Nathpanthis Siddhas And Yogis.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Puranic Hinduism and Buddhism/Jainism
